1. Agent or provider system prompt
2. Built-in environment and date context
3. Code Mode tool guidance, when enabled
4. Global and project AGENTS.md files
5. Available skill, reference, and MCP guidance

"""One-off: measure Pollinations' rate limit so the backoff is not a guess.

Fires the real endpoint back-to-back, then again with increasing gaps, and
reports the HTTP status for each attempt.
"""

import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from qf_visuals.photo import photo_url

PROMPT = "a teacup on a wooden counter, vertical cinematic photo, no text"


def probe(gap: float, n: int) -> list[tuple[float, int, str]]:
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        if i:
            time.sleep(gap)
        url = photo_url(f"{PROMPT} probe {int(time.time() * 1000) % 100000} {i}")
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "qf-pipeline/0.1"})
        t0 = time.time()
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
                body = r.read()
                out.append((gap, r.status, f"{len(body) // 1024}KB in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s"))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            out.append((gap, e.code, f"HTTPError after {time.time() - t0:.1f}s"))
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            out.append((gap, -1, f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:60]}"))
    return out


print("=== burst: 5 requests, no gap ===")

"""Verify the slideshow fix: frames inside a single beat must now differ.

Before the fix, a beat held one still for its whole duration, so any two frames
inside the same beat were pixel-identical. This script measures that directly
instead of eyeballing it, and also checks the dissolve at a beat boundary.

Usage: python check_motion.py <video.mp4>
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

# Beat boundaries from copy.py: 0.0 3.1 6.6 10.1 13.6 17.1, each ~3.5s long.
INSIDE_BEAT = [0.4, 1.4, 2.4, 3.0]  # all within beat 0 (0.0-3.5)
AROUND_CUT = [6.3, 6.6, 6.9]  # beat 1 -> beat 2 backdrop change at 6.6


def grab(video: str, t: float, dest: Path) -> np.ndarray:
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "ffmpeg", "-y", "-loglevel", "quiet", "-ss", f"{t}",
            "-i", video, "-frames:v", "1", "-update", "1", str(dest),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    return np.asarray(Image.open(dest).convert("L"), dtype=np.float32)


def mean_abs_diff(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:
    return float(np.abs(a - b).mean())


def main() -> int:
    video = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "storage/videos/show-chai.mp4"
    tmp = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "qfchk2"

    print(f"video: {video}")

    print("\n-- inside beat 0 (0.4s .. 3.0s) --")
    print("   a still backdrop would report 0.00 for every pair")
    frames = {t: grab(video, t, tmp / f"in_{t}.png") for t in INSIDE_BEAT}
    worst = 0.0
    for i, t1 in enumerate(INSIDE_BEAT):
        for t2 in INSIDE_BEAT[i + 1:]:
            d = mean_abs_diff(frames[t1], frames[t2])
            worst = max(worst, d)
            print(f"   t={t1:>4}s vs t={t2:>4}s  mean|diff| = {d:6.2f}")
    span = mean_abs_diff(frames[INSIDE_BEAT[0]], frames[INSIDE_BEAT[-1]])
    print(f"   full-beat span t={INSIDE_BEAT[0]} -> t={INSIDE_BEAT[-1]} = {span:6.2f}")

    print("\n-- across the 6.6s cut (dissolve) --")
    cut = {t: grab(video, t, tmp / f"cut_{t}.png") for t in AROUND_CUT}
    print(f"   t=6.3 -> 6.6  {mean_abs_diff(cut[6.3], cut[6.6]):6.2f}   (hard cut if large)")
    print(f"   t=6.6 -> 6.9  {mean_abs_diff(cut[6.6], cut[6.9]):6.2f}")

    print("\n-- verdict --")
    moving = worst > 0.5
    print(f"   intra-beat motion: {'MOVING (fix works)' if moving else 'STILL (fix did NOT work)'}")
    if not moving:
        print("   every pair inside a beat is identical -> still a slideshow")
    return 0 if moving else 1

    raise SystemExit(main())

# Backdrop motion. Backdrops are still photos, so without this they read as a
    # slideshow: one frame held for 6.6s. Ken Burns (linear scale + pan across the
    # whole beat) makes a still drift like a camera move instead of sitting dead,
    # and the zoom direction alternates so it does not read as a loop.
    #
    # The backdrop must stay fully opaque. hyperframes paints a .clip only inside
    # its own data-start/data-duration window, so consecutive clips do not overlap
    # and there is nothing to crossfade into: fading a backdrop up from 0 just
    # dips the frame to black for the length of the fade. Beats are butt-jointed,
    # so the swap is a cut, and it is masked the same way the content is -- the
    # incoming backdrop resolves out of a blur.
    for bi, (start, dur, _c, _p, _k) in enumerate(beats):
        if not bgmap[bi]:
            continue
        zoom_in = bi % 2 == 0
        s0, s1 = (1.08, 1.2) if zoom_in else (1.2, 1.08)
        dx = -26 if bi % 4 < 2 else 26
